name: Nicaragua
snapshot: Daniel Ortega and his wife Rosario Murillo now rule as co-presidents, preparing an open family succession as rumours about his health swirl.
culture: Nicaragua calls itself the land of poets, and Rubén Darío, father of Spanish-language modernism, is a national hero. Its Caribbean coast is home to Miskito, Creole and Garifuna communities with their own languages and autonomy. The Masaya volcano, Granada's colonial streets and surf beaches draw visitors.
society: Since 2018 protests in which some 300 people died, the government has closed thousands of NGOs, seized universities, expelled priests and stripped hundreds of critics of citizenship. Hundreds of thousands have emigrated. The economy relies on remittances, gold, coffee and trade with the US under a free trade agreement.
situation: Daniel Ortega first came to power as the revolutionary who overthrew the Somoza family dictatorship in 1979. In 2026, at 80, he presided over something that looks a lot like what he fought: a family dynasty. Since a 2025 constitutional rewrite, his wife Rosario Murillo has been officially "co-president," decrees carry both their signatures, and the presidential term is six years (Infobae).

At the 19 July anniversary of the revolution, observers noted how slowly and stiffly Ortega walked, feeding long rumours about his health and the question of what happens when he dies, with Murillo and their children placed throughout the state. In the same week he said there would be no more elections in Nicaragua, so the opposition could never "capture" power (El Financiero). Three days earlier, Nicaragua broke off relations with Italy; one exiled critic claimed it followed failed talks to secure European guarantees for members of the family. Washington, after seizing Venezuela's Maduro in January, called Murillo's co-presidency invented and illegitimate, which reportedly unsettled Managua. The repression is old by now: thousands of NGOs closed, universities and churches seized, critics stripped of citizenship and expelled since the 2018 protests in which some 300 people died. What is new is the frankness. Nicaragua no longer pretends to be heading anywhere but a succession.
power: Formally a presidential republic, in practice a one-family dictatorship. The co-presidents control the Sandinista party, the National Assembly, the courts, the electoral council, the police and the army, and since 2025 the constitution subordinates all branches to the presidency.
holders: Co-presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo.
